description: RaoSpace Labs is a multidisciplinary team focused on applying AI, data science, software engineering, and scientific research to real-world challenges. We aim to build innovative solutions using NASA's open data, satellite imagery, machine learning, and geospatial analysis. Our interests include Earth observation, climate monitoring, disaster response, space exploration. We welcome developers, AI/ML enthusiasts, data scientists, designers, and researchers who want to create meaningful solutions.
summary: IGNIS (Space Combustion Intelligence) is an evidence-grounded, multi-agent scientific research system developed by RaoSpace Labs for NASA's microgravity combustion and spacecraft fire-safety challenge. Built using Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), IGNIS transforms NASA combustion research into searchable, structured, and interpretable scientific evidence. It combines NASA literature discovery, document intelligence, hybrid retrieval, experimental-condition extraction, statistical analysis, machine-learning suitability assessment, knowledge-graph extraction, and scientific review. Its research corpus contains approximately 102 unique documents, 16,168 page-anchored chunks, and 5,444 PDF pages. Researchers can investigate combustion experiments, compare findings, examine experimental conditions, and explore potential relevance to spacecraft, lunar, and Mars missions. IGNIS preserves source references and explicitly distinguishes measured findings from interpretations and unverified mission implications. Its goal is to make decades of space-combustion research more accessible and useful for evidence-informed fire-safety research.
details:
Project Overview

IGNIS — Space Combustion Intelligence is an evidence-grounded, multi-agent scientific research system designed to help researchers explore NASA microgravity combustion research and investigate its relevance to spacecraft fire safety.

The project addresses a central research challenge: valuable findings about combustion in microgravity are distributed across scientific publications, investigation reports, and technical documents. Finding relevant evidence, understanding experimental conditions, and comparing results across different investigations can be difficult and time-consuming.

IGNIS brings these research capabilities together in one coordinated system.

How It Works

IGNIS uses Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) to coordinate a root research orchestrator and eight specialist capabilities:

  • NASA Research Agent: discovers investigations, publications, reports, and research metadata.
  • Document Intelligence Agent: extracts experimental conditions, materials, methods, measurements, and findings from research documents.
  • Data Analyst Agent: performs deterministic statistical analysis using Python-based tools.
  • Machine Learning Agent: assesses dataset suitability and recommends appropriate algorithms, features, and evaluation strategies.
  • Knowledge Graph Agent: extracts scientific entities and relationships into graph-ready structures.
  • Multimodal Agent: analyzes scientific figures, plots, charts, and images when a suitable vision model is configured.
  • Fire Safety Agent: examines potential relevance to ISS, lunar, Mars, and deep-space missions.
  • Scientific Reviewer: checks evidence support, citations, unsupported claims, and research limitations.

A programmatic workflow engine coordinates research discovery, experiment comparison, ML suitability, scientific questions, knowledge-graph extraction, figure analysis, and statistical analysis.

NASA Research and Retrieval

IGNIS includes a local research corpus assembled from NASA Technical Reports Server material. The documented corpus snapshot contains approximately 102 unique documents, 16,168 page-anchored chunks, and 5,444 PDF pages, alongside a 30-question gold evaluation set.

Research areas include BASS/BASS-II, FLEX, ACME, SAME/SAME-R, SAFFIRE, CIR, FLAME-SPREAD, FLAMMABILITY, COOL-FLAMES, SMOKE-DET, MAT-FLAM, and FIRE-SAFETY.

The retrieval system combines TF-IDF sparse search, dense MiniLM embeddings, title-overlap boosting, investigation filtering, and page-level evidence anchors. This helps researchers trace retrieved information back to its source documents and relevant pages.

Scientific Analysis and Integrity

IGNIS supports descriptive statistics, missing-value analysis, group comparisons, correlation analysis, and numerical summaries. It also assesses whether available data is appropriate for machine-learning applications rather than assuming that every dataset supports reliable prediction.

A dedicated scientific-review stage helps identify unsupported claims, missing evidence, citation problems, and conclusions requiring expert review.

The system distinguishes:

  1. What an experiment actually measured.
  2. What the findings may suggest.
  3. How those findings might be relevant to a space mission.
  4. What remains untested or unverified.

Technology Stack

  • Python
  • Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
  • Groq-hosted language models through LiteLLM
  • TF-IDF and MiniLM dense embeddings
  • Pandas and NumPy
  • Scientific document processing and retrieval tools
  • PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV, and JSON support

The system provides an interactive ADK developer interface and a command-line interface. Its capabilities depend on the configured model credentials and available services.

Creativity and Innovation

IGNIS combines multi-agent orchestration with NASA-specific research retrieval, page-anchored evidence, deterministic scientific analysis, investigation comparison, and a dedicated scientific-review layer.

Rather than treating a language model's answer as scientific proof, IGNIS is designed to preserve experimental context, provide traceable references, and communicate uncertainty.

Intended Impact

IGNIS aims to make microgravity combustion research easier to discover, compare, and interpret. It can support researchers investigating flame behavior, material combustion, smoke, and suppression, while helping identify evidence gaps relevant to future spacecraft, lunar habitats, and Mars missions.

IGNIS is a scientific research and decision-support prototype. It does not certify spacecraft systems, approve materials, or replace expert fire-safety testing.
